design_gaps.needed: Q-022 is unanswered. We need to know what happens when no representative has a matching skill or when several do (for example a fallback queue, workload balancing or round robin), and who maintains representatives' skills. The design assumes matching on issue category only (ASM-010).

Q-015 is unanswered. We need the configuring role and a definition of 'without major redevelopment'. The design assumes an administrator makes the change declaratively in Setup with no code deployment. Q-011 is also unanswered, so the initial category list is still needed.

Q-015 and Q-010 are unanswered. We need the configuring role, the definition of 'without major redevelopment', and the allowed status transitions. We also need to confirm how renaming or removing statuses that automation depends on (for example Resolved for escalation and auto-close, and Closed) should be handled.

Q-015 is unanswered. We need the configuring role and the definition of 'without major redevelopment'. We also need to confirm whether a changed timeframe applies to requests that are already open or only to new ones.

Q-015 is unanswered. We need the configuring role and the definition of 'without major redevelopment'. We also need to know what a 'notification rule' may change: the triggering events, the channels (email and portal), the message content, and whether each rule can be switched on or off.

Mandatory form fields and permitted attachment file types, maximum size and count (acceptance criteria are TBC; Q-011). Also whether customers must log in to submit and how portal accounts are created (Q-024), which determines whether the form is a guest-user site page.
Matching criteria for identifying existing customers and properties (e.g. email, phone, address) and the handling of uncertain matches (acceptance criterion is TBC; Q-014).

Membership and maintenance of the designated escalation team, whether the original representative stays involved after escalation, and whether the 5-day timer restarts for requests created after dissatisfaction (Q-021). The design can proceed with a single configurable queue, but the queue's members must be confirmed.

The acceptance criterion contains '<TBC: allowed status transitions>'. The allowed status transitions are needed, along with whether any changes are automatic (Q-010), before transition validation can be designed.

Clarification of how an appointment is scheduled and recorded, and by whom, is needed so the appointment-scheduled notification has a defined trigger (Q-012). Confirmation is also needed of whether 'additional information required' is signalled only by the Awaiting Customer Information status or by a separate action.

A portal notification requires the customer to have a portal user at submission time. It must be confirmed whether customers log in to submit, or how and when portal accounts are created (Q-024), so the portal acknowledgement can be delivered.

Q-023 is unanswered. The design needs to know whether representatives and maintenance team members can view, read-only, requests that are not theirs. The answer decides the org-wide default (Private or Public Read Only) and the sharing rules. Also confirm whether any administrator role exists beyond the four named roles.

Q-025 is unanswered. Confirm whether employees may close a request manually, or whether a request may be reopened, during the 6 weeks after a satisfactory response. This decides whether the scheduled auto-close must re-check status. Also confirm the handling when the customer never responds to the confirmation request.

solution_design.automation:
**Flows (declarative first)**
- *Case before-save*: stamps Escalation_Due__c as CreatedDate plus Request_Setting__mdt days.
- *Case after-save*:
  - Scheduled path at Escalation_Due__c: if Status is not Resolved or Closed, assign to the Escalation queue and set Is_Escalated__c.
  - Notification dispatcher: evaluates Notification_Rule__mdt for submission, status change, Awaiting Customer Information, appointment set and Resolved, then sends the email template and custom notification.
  - Rating handler: a rating of 1–2 closes the case and creates a child Case at New with ParentId set (ASM-014). A rating of 3–5 stamps Satisfaction_Response_Date__c.
  - Scheduled path at Satisfaction_Response_Date__c plus 42 days: closes the case if it is still Resolved.
- *Screen flows*: Request Information, Send Reminder, Confirm Resolution, Assign Maintenance Team, and the portal Rate Request flow.

**Apex (one trigger per object with a handler class)**
- *CaseTrigger / CaseTriggerHandler*: opens and closes Request_Assignment__c periods on owner change, team change and close.
- *FeedItemTrigger / FeedItemTriggerHandler*: an external-visible post by a CSR sends an email and portal notification to the customer. A portal post notifies the owner.
- *MaintenanceRequestIntakeService*: guest intake.
- *Omni-Channel*: a routing configuration and skills map Issue_Category__c through Category_Skill__mdt.

All Apex is bulk-safe for 200 records. Tests use TestDataFactory.

solution_design.context:
Reel Estate property developers need a maintenance request service covering 32 approved REQs. Customers submit requests through a public website form (the only intake channel, ASM-005). Requests are routed automatically to customer service representatives (CSRs) by skill, handed to maintenance teams, and progressed through a configurable lifecycle. Customers, both owners and tenants (ASM-001), track their own requests, exchange messages, respond to information requests and rate resolution in an authenticated Experience Cloud portal. The system escalates unresolved requests after 5 calendar days, auto-closes requests 6 weeks after a satisfactory rating, and creates a linked child request on a rating of 1 or 2. Managers report on all requests, workload, overdue items, resolution time per assignment period and satisfaction.

The solution is built on **Service Cloud** (standard Case with a *Maintenance Request* record type), **Omni-Channel skills-based routing**, **Experience Cloud** (Customer Community licence), record-triggered Flows, a small amount of Apex where Flow cannot reach (guest intake, FeedItem events, assignment-period tracking), Custom Metadata for configurability, and standard reports and dashboards. No org snapshot was supplied, so every component is assumed new. There are no external integrations.
solution_design.data_model:
**Case** (record type *Maintenance Request*) is the request. New fields:
- Issue_Category__c (picklist backed by a global value set)
- Property__c (lookup)
- Preferred_Appointment__c (DateTime)
- Appointment_DateTime__c (DateTime)
- Maintenance_Team__c (picklist)
- Escalation_Due__c (DateTime, stamped on create)
- Is_Overdue__c (formula: NOW() past Escalation_Due__c and Status not Resolved or Closed)
- Satisfaction_Rating__c (Number 1–5, validated)
- Satisfaction_Response_Date__c (DateTime)
- Is_Escalated__c (Checkbox)

The standard ParentId field links child requests to their original. Standard Status holds the lifecycle values from REQ-009.

**Customer**: Contact under an individual Account, enabled as a Customer Community user.

**Property__c**: address fields. **Property_Customer__c**: junction (Contact, Property, Relationship picklist Owner/Tenant), giving a many-to-many model.

**Request_Assignment__c** (master-detail to Case):
- Assignment_Type__c (Representative/Team)
- Assignee_User__c
- Team__c
- Start__c, End__c
- Duration_Hours__c (formula)

**Custom Metadata**:
- Request_Setting__mdt (Escalation_Days__c = 5, Auto_Close_Days__c = 42)
- Category_Skill__mdt (category to Omni skill)
- Notification_Rule__mdt (event, status, email template, notification type, active)

Files are stored as ContentVersion linked to the Case.

decisions.decision: Use the standard Case object as the maintenance request.
decisions.rationale: Case provides Status and Support Process, Omni-Channel routing, feed, sharing sets, history and portal components out of the box.

decisions.alternatives: Apex round-robin with skill matching from metadata, or assignment rules to queues.
decisions.decision: Use Omni-Channel skills-based routing for automatic CSR assignment.
decisions.rationale: It meets the skill-matching requirement (ASM-010) declaratively, and assignment rules cannot match individual users' skills.

decisions.alternatives: Standard Case Escalation Rules, or a daily scheduled flow or batch.
decisions.decision: Drive escalation from a stamped Escalation_Due__c field and a Flow scheduled path, with days held in Custom Metadata.
decisions.rationale: A single metadata value drives both escalation and the overdue flag with near-exact timing, and avoids keeping two separately configured thresholds in step.

decisions.alternatives: Change the owner to a team queue, or use Case Teams or Apex manual sharing.
decisions.decision: Model maintenance team assignment as a Case picklist with criteria-based sharing to team groups, keeping ownership with the CSR.
decisions.rationale: The CSR keeps ownership and communication while team members gain the edit access required by ASM-011, all declaratively.

decisions.decision: Model customers as Contact plus an individual Account, rather than enabling Person Accounts.
decisions.rationale: Enabling Person Accounts is irreversible org-wide and needs Technical Architect sign-off without an org snapshot, while Contact-based users fully support the portal and sharing set.

decisions.alternatives: Case Comments with IsPublished, or a custom Request_Message__c object.
decisions.decision: Use Case Feed visibility for customer messages and internal notes.
decisions.rationale: Feed natively separates internal and external visibility, is supported in the portal and supports Apex triggers for notifications.

decisions.alternatives: Web-to-Case HTML form, or a guest OmniScript.
decisions.decision: Host the intake form as a guest LWC on Experience Cloud rather than using Web-to-Case.
decisions.rationale: Web-to-Case cannot handle attachments or customer and property matching, and an LWC keeps the guest surface small without an OmniStudio licence dependency.

decisions.alternatives: Reporting on Case history, or Case Milestones and Entitlements.
decisions.decision: Track resolution time in a Request_Assignment__c child object maintained by Apex.
decisions.rationale: Neither history reports nor milestones produce one reportable duration per assignee period, which ASM-013 requires.

solution_design.integration: No external system integrations are required by the approved requirements. Email is sent from Salesforce through an org-wide email address and Lightning email templates. Portal notifications use Custom Notification Types delivered to Experience Cloud users. Customer email replies are not in scope as an inbound channel. Customers respond through the portal (REQ-007), so Email-to-Case is not configured. The public intake form is hosted on Experience Cloud and reached from the company website by link or embed, so no API integration with the website CMS is planned. No Named Credentials, callouts or middleware are needed. If the website team later requires a native embed or server-to-server submission, that would be a new requirement.
solution_design.non_functional:
**Volumes**: not stated. The design assumes moderate service volumes. All Apex and Flow logic is bulk-safe at 200 records and performs no SOQL or DML in loops. Scheduled paths are subject to platform limits on flow interviews per hour, which is acceptable at expected volumes. This should be confirmed with the client.

**Limits**:
- Field history tracking allows 20 fields per object, and history is retained for 18–24 months. Longer retention would need Field Audit Trail (reviewer decision).
- Guest file uploads are subject to size limits and require the guest upload setting.
- Omni-Channel routes only to CSRs who are online. Unrouted requests wait in the routing queue.

**Abuse**: the public form has no authentication, so spam is a risk. Server-side validation is included. CAPTCHA or rate limiting would be a reviewer suggestion, not in scope.

**Accessibility**: WCAG 2.1 AA for custom UI.

**Audit** (REQ-021): Status, Owner, Maintenance_Team__c, Satisfaction_Rating__c, Appointment_DateTime__c and Is_Escalated__c are history-tracked. Feed, email messages and assignment periods complete the trail.

**Time**: escalation and auto-close use calendar time (ASM-008, ASM-018). No business hours apply.

**Configurability**:
- Categories, statuses, teams, escalation days and notification rules are changed through picklists and Custom Metadata (REQ-026 to REQ-029).
- A change to escalation days applies to requests created after the change.
solution_design.security_model:
**Case OWD**: Private internally and externally. Grant Access Using Hierarchies is retained but not relied on.

**Employees** (REQ-023, ASM-011):
- CSRs edit only the requests they own.
- Maintenance team members get Read/Write through criteria-based sharing rules (Maintenance_Team__c = team) to one public group per team.
- Supervisors and managers get Read/Write to all Maintenance Request cases through a criteria-based rule to a Supervisors & Managers group, so View All or Modify All is not needed (REQ-016).

**Customers** (REQ-022, REQ-032): Customer Community users see only cases where ContactId matches their contact, through a sharing set. Portal pages require authentication. Internal feed posts and internal-only fields are hidden by feed visibility and FLS.

**Guest user** (REQ-001): access is limited to the intake page. The intake Apex class runs *without sharing* only inside a narrowly scoped service that matches the Contact and Property and creates the Case. This is a documented, reviewed exception. Input is validated server-side, and the service returns no record data to the guest.

**Permission sets** (least privilege): CSR, Maintenance Team Member, Supervisor/Manager, Portal Customer, Request Admin (metadata and picklist configuration). Apex defaults to *with sharing* and uses WITH USER_MODE or Security.stripInaccessible. There are no hardcoded IDs: queues and groups are resolved by DeveloperName.
solution_design.ui:
**Internal users**: a Lightning Service Console app with Omni-Channel presence for CSRs. A Maintenance Request Case record page (FlexiPage) shows highlights, a status path, the feed with an internal/customer visibility toggle, files, related Property and customer, child requests, assignment periods and history. Quick actions are visible by permission set. Managers have a dashboard tab.

**Public intake**: an LWC form on an Experience Cloud public page, linked from or embedded in the company website. It captures name, email, phone, property address, category, description, preferred appointment time and files (lightning-file-upload). It provides client-side and server-side validation and a confirmation screen with a reference number.

**Customer portal** (Customer Service template, authenticated):
- My Requests list and request detail
- Customer-visible feed for messages and replies
- File upload
- Notification bell
- Rate Request screen flow, shown when Status is Resolved and the rating is blank

**Accessibility**: all custom UI targets WCAG 2.1 AA. LWCs use base components and labelled inputs, and validation messages are announced.

suggestions: Add a fallback unassigned-request queue for requests with no skill-matched representative. This is pending the answer to Q-022 and is not in scope until confirmed.
Balance workload among several matching representatives, for example by assigning to the one with the fewest open requests. This is pending the answer to Q-022.
Have the requests created on a 1 or 2 rating (REQ-014) reuse the same skill-based assignment, so routing is consistent. This is to be confirmed when REQ-014 is designed.
Add duplicate and matching rules for customers and properties once the REQ-025 matching criteria are confirmed. No current REQ requires automatic duplicate blocking.
Consider a portal list view of all of a customer's requests with filtering by property. REQ-006 only requires viewing a request's current status.
Consider sending a pre-escalation warning to the assigned CSR before the 5-day threshold. No REQ asks for this.
Consider automatic, scheduled reminders in addition to manual reminders, pending the answer to Q-013.

Avoid duplicate notifications when one event matches several REQ-015 triggers, for example a change to Resolved, which is both a status change and a resolution. The approver should confirm whether a single combined notification is acceptable.
Add an average-resolution-time-per-assignee summary to the manager dashboard. This is not explicitly required by REQ-019.
Add workload threshold alerts for managers. This is not required by REQ-017.
Allow only one satisfaction rating per resolution confirmation and lock the rating after submission, to prevent repeat submissions creating duplicate linked requests. No approved REQ requires this.
Define how portal accounts are provisioned (self-registration or invitation after the first request), per Q-024. REQ-032 assumes customers already hold credentials.
Consider a rating comment field so customers can explain a low rating. No approved REQ requires this.

components.specification:
Declared public with sharing. Method: public static void routeNewRequests(List<Case> cases).
1. Filter to Maintenance_Request record type Cases (resolved by DeveloperName) that have Issue_Category__c set.
2. Load active Category_Skill__mdt records once.
3. Query Skills by DeveloperName once.
4. Insert PendingServiceRouting records with IsReadyForRouting=false, RoutingType='SkillsBased', the CMP-005 ServiceChannelId resolved by DeveloperName, RoutingModel='MostAvailable', CapacityWeight=1, and WorkItemId set to the Case.
5. Insert SkillRequirement records.
6. Update the PendingServiceRouting records to IsReadyForRouting=true.
All DML is bulk (single DML per step). A Case with an unmapped category is left unrouted, and a warning is logged through System.debug or the project logger. There are no hardcoded Ids.

components.specification: A with sharing class. afterInsert(List<FeedItem>) filters to posts that meet all of these: ParentId is a Case, Visibility = 'AllUsers', Type is TextPost or ContentPost, and the poster is an internal (Standard) user. It queries the parent cases WITH USER_MODE and keeps those with RecordType DeveloperName Maintenance_Request, CreatedById equal to Case.OwnerId (the assigned representative) and ContactId populated. Update Records: OwnerId = queue Id and Is_Escalated__c = true. A fault path logs the error and posts nothing to the customer. Runs in system context. components.specification:
This class is declared without sharing. It is the documented guest exception and is called only by CMP-048.

Public method: static String submit(IntakeRequest req, List<FileInput> files). It returns the CaseNumber only.

Server-side validation:
- Mandatory fields per the TBC list, held in a constant set.
- Email and phone format.
- Category is a valid Issue_Category value.
- File extension, size and count checked against Request_Setting__mdt.Default.
It throws IntakeValidationException carrying field-level messages.

Matching and record creation:
- Matches Contact by email. If there is no match, it creates an individual Account and a Contact.
- Matches Property__c by normalised street and postal code. If there is no match, it creates one.
- Upserts Property_Customer__c, avoiding duplicates.
- Inserts a Case with the Maintenance_Request record type (resolved by DeveloperName), SuppliedName, SuppliedEmail, SuppliedPhone, ContactId, Property__c, Issue_Category__c, Description and Preferred_Appointment__c.
- Inserts a ContentVersion for each file with FirstPublishLocationId set to the Case.

All DML runs in a single transaction with a savepoint and rollback on failure.

- @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) static Map<String,Object> getIntakeConfig(): returns the allowed extensions, maximum file size, maximum file count, Issue_Category picklist values and the mandatory field list for client-side validation.

This class is declared with sharing.

Invocable method: @InvocableMethod sendNotifications(List<Request>). Each Request carries caseId and eventName (Submitted or Status_Changed).

Bulk-safe behaviour:
- Queries active Notification_Rule__mdt records once.
- Queries the cases with ContactId and Status once.
- Queries the portal Users for those contacts once.
- For each rule matching the event and, if set, the Status, it builds a SingleEmailMessage. The template is resolved by DeveloperName, the target is the Contact, the What is the Case, and the sender is the OrgWideEmailAddress resolved by address.
- It sends a Messaging.CustomNotification, with the type resolved by DeveloperName, to the portal user.
- It makes a single Messaging.sendEmail call.

Missing templates, types or users are logged and skipped without failing the transaction. Because rules are read at runtime, edits apply on the next event.

components.specification:
Declared public inherited sharing. Public methods:
- onAfterInsert(List<Case> newCases): for Maintenance Request cases (record type resolved by DeveloperName), opens a Representative period when the owner is a User (OwnerId starts with 005), and opens a Team period when Maintenance_Team__c is set. Start__c is CreatedDate.
- onAfterUpdate(List<Case> newCases, Map<Id,Case> oldMap): on an owner change, closes the open Representative period (End__c = now) and opens a new one if the new owner is a User. On a Maintenance_Team__c change, does the same for Team periods. When IsClosed becomes true, sets End__c = ClosedDate on all open periods and opens none.

Uses one SOQL query and one DML statement per operation, so it is bulk-safe for 200 records. DML uses AccessLevel.SYSTEM_MODE because periods are system audit data that users must not edit; this is a documented exception. CaseTriggerHandler (CMP-007) must call both methods.

risk_flags: Mixed DML between setup objects (User, GroupMember) and Case requires separate runAs blocks.
components.specification: @IsTest class using TestDataFactory. Users: CSR1 and CSR2 with Maintenance_CSR (CMP-016) in peer roles; TeamA and TeamB members with Maintenance_Team_Member (CMP-128) added to their team groups (CMP-126); and a Supervisor in the Maintenance_Supervisors_Managers group (CMP-066) with CMP-068. Cases are owned by CSR1 and CSR2, with Maintenance_Team__c set to TeamA or TeamB. Assertions use System.runAs together with UserRecordAccess queries and DML attempts. CSR1 can edit their own case and cannot edit CSR2's. TeamA can edit TeamA cases and cannot edit TeamB cases. The supervisor can read and edit all cases.
components.tests: Scenarios cover all three acceptance criteria. Bulk scenario: 200 TeamA cases are all editable by TeamA and none by TeamB. Negative paths assert insufficient access errors. Uses criteria rule recalculation, which is synchronous in tests.
